terminal.description: A shell in the top folder. Run the setup once to build the shop's folder, then go into shop and work there with git.

tasks.title: Make the shop's folder a repository
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs` in the top folder first. It builds `shop`, the folder that holds the shop's website: four files and no history.

Turn `shop` into a Git repository, so Git can start keeping its history. Make the repository in `shop` itself, not in the top folder above it.

The check looks for the `.git` folder inside `shop`.
nextSteps: Run `node setup.mjs` in the top folder, then move into `shop`.
Run `git status` once: Git says the folder is not a repository yet.
Make the repository with the command from the lesson.
Run `git status` again. It now talks about commits and untracked files.
hints: The terminal starts in the top folder, which holds setup.mjs. The shop's folder is one level down.
Git makes the repository in the folder the terminal is in. Move into shop with `cd` before you make it.
From the top folder run `cd shop`, then `git init`.

tasks.title: Tell Git who you are in this repository
tasks.description:
Every commit records who made it. Set your name and an email address in the settings of the `shop` repository only. A made-up address is fine.

Do not add `--global`: that would change the settings for every repository on this computer, and this course keeps its settings inside each repository.

The check reads `user.name` and `user.email` from the settings of `shop` itself. The name must not be empty, and the email needs an `@` and no spaces.
nextSteps: Make sure the terminal is inside `shop`.
Set `user.name` with `git config`, putting a name with a space in quotes.
Read each one back with `git config user.name` and `git config user.email`.
hints: Both settings are made with one command, `git config`, run inside shop.
`git config` takes the name of the setting first and its value after it. A value with a space goes in double quotes.
Run `git config user.name "Your Name"`, then `git config user.email "you@example.com"`, with your own values.

tasks.title: Save the whole site in a first commit
tasks.description:
Save the site exactly as Femi left it in one first commit. That commit must hold all four files: `finds.html`, `index.html`, `style.css` and `visit.html`. Do not change any of them before this commit.

The check reads the first commit in the history of `shop` and lists the files in it.
nextSteps: Run `git status` and read which files Git lists as untracked.
Add every file to the staging area.
Run `git status` again: the files are now under changes to be committed.
Commit with a short message, given with `-m`.
hints: A commit holds only what is in the staging area, so all four files have to be added first.
`git add` takes file names, and `.` stands for everything in the folder you are in. Then `git commit` with `-m` and a message in quotes.
Run `git add .` and then `git commit -m "Add the website as Femi left it"`.

tasks.title: Change the Saturday hours in a commit of their own
tasks.description:
Wilma opens at 9:00 on Saturdays now, not 10:00. Closing time stays 17:00. Open `shop/visit.html` in the editor, change the opening time on the Saturday line and save. Then commit that change as a second commit.

The check finds the commit where `visit.html` starts opening at 9:00 on Saturdays. It expects the commit before it to still say 10:00, the Saturday line to still close at 17:00, every other line of `visit.html` to be as it was, and no other file in that commit.
nextSteps: Open `shop/visit.html` from the files panel and change only the Saturday opening time. Save.
Run `git status`: Git lists `visit.html` as modified.
Stage that file and commit it with a message that says what changed.
Run `git log --oneline`: there are now two commits.
hints: This change goes through the same two steps as the first commit: stage, then commit.
Saving in the editor changes only the working folder. Git needs `git add visit.html` before the commit can hold it.
Run `git add visit.html`, then `git commit -m "Open at 9:00 on Saturdays"`.
